remove.bodyWithBranch: This deletes the folder {path}, and the branch {branch} too if git finds it merged.

removeAnyway.bodyDetached: It has uncommitted changes, which will be lost.

lockPrompt.body: A locked worktree is never pruned and cannot be removed until it is unlocked.

worktrees.removedBranchFailed: Removed worktree {folder}; git refused to delete the branch {name}. {message}
worktrees.removedBranchNoHost: Removed worktree {folder}. The branch {name} stays: no other worktree is left to delete it from.

dialogs.createBody: From {start}. The branch is checked out unless you untick it.
dialogs.name: Name
dialogs.deleteBody: The branch is deleted; its commits stay in the graph as long as another ref or the reflog reaches them.
dialogs.deleteAnywayBody: git refused: the branch is not fully merged. Its commits stay reachable through the reflog for 90 days (git reflog, then git branch).
dialogs.upstreamBody: The remote branch the branch pulls from and pushes to; none clears it.
dialogs.tagBody: A lightweight tag, or an annotated one with a message.
dialogs.resetBody: {branch} moves to {rev}. A hard reset also drops the uncommitted changes in the working tree. The reflog keeps the previous HEAD for 90 days (git reflog, then git reset).
dialogs.undoCommitBody: {hash} is on {remote} already. Undoing it here leaves it there, so your next push of this branch needs a forced push; Revert undoes it with a new commit instead. The reflog keeps the commit: git reset --soft {hash} brings it back.
dialogs.resetBodyChanges: {branch} moves to {rev}. A hard reset also drops the {n} uncommitted change in the working tree. The reflog keeps the previous HEAD for 90 days (git reflog, then git reset). | {branch} moves to {rev}. A hard reset also drops the {n} uncommitted changes in the working tree. The reflog keeps the previous HEAD for 90 days (git reflog, then git reset).
dialogs.softHint: keeps the index and the working tree
dialogs.mixedHint: keeps the working tree, unstages everything
dialogs.hardHint: drops the index and the working tree changes
dialogs.dirtySwitchBody: git refused to switch to {name}: your local changes would be overwritten. Stash them (untracked files included), switch, then pop the stash when you are back.
dialogs.deleteTagBody: The tag is deleted. Tags have no reflog: the toast keeps its hash, and git tag brings it back until git gc runs.
dialogs.onRemoteConsequence: {name} leaves {remote} for everyone who uses it; the toast keeps the command that puts it back.
dialogs.heldTitle: {branch} is checked out in another worktree
dialogs.heldBody: A branch is checked out in one worktree at a time: {branch} is in {folder}.

cleanup.title: Clean up branches
cleanup.body: Branches merged into {main}, or gone from their remote. A branch's worktree goes with it, its folder deleted with the files git ignores in it; the toast keeps the commands that bring each branch back.
cleanup.empty: Nothing to clean up: no branch is merged into {main} or gone from its remote.
cleanup.noMain: Nothing to compare with: no main or master branch, and origin/HEAD names none here. git remote set-head origin --auto sets it from the remote.
cleanup.confirmWithWorktree: Delete {n} branch and its worktree | Delete {n} branches and 1 worktree

reason.upstreamApplied: Its upstream is gone, its changes in {main}
reason.upstreamGone: Its upstream is gone, not in {main}
reason.upstreamUnchecked: Its upstream is gone, not checked against {main}

cleanup.deletedWithWorktree: Deleted {n} branch and 1 worktree | Deleted {n} branches and 1 worktree
cleanup.deletedWithWorktrees: Deleted {n} branch and {m} worktrees | Deleted {n} branches and {m} worktrees

kept.moved: {names} stayed: it has commits since it was listed | {names} stayed: they have commits since they were listed
kept.missing: {names} was deleted elsewhere already | {names} were deleted elsewhere already
kept.worktree-moved: {names} stayed: its worktree has another branch checked out now | {names} stayed: their worktrees have other branches checked out now
kept.worktree: {names} stayed: git refused to remove its worktree | {names} stayed: git refused to remove their worktrees
kept.failed: {names} stayed: git refused to delete it | {names} stayed: git refused to delete them
kept.stopped: {names} stayed: the cleanup stopped before it | {names} stayed: the cleanup stopped before them

cleanup.failed: Could not clean up the branches: {message}
cleanup.busy: The cleanup is still deleting branches. Try again when it ends.

banner.hint: Resolve the files, mark them, then continue.
banner.hintClean: Every conflict is marked resolved; continue or abort.
banner.abortBody: The operation's changes are dropped and the working tree returns to where it was before it started.

side.body: {lost}, and any edit made to it since the conflict, go, and the file is marked resolved. Undo in the toast brings the conflict back.
side.bodyDeleted: {lost}, and any edit made to it since the conflict, go: the file is deleted, as {holder} has no version of it, and marked resolved. Undo in the toast brings the conflict back.
side.takeFailed: Couldn't use a side's version of {path}. {message}
side.undoFailed: Couldn't bring back the conflict of {path}. {message}

remotes.title: Remotes
remotes.name: Name
remotes.empty: No remotes. Add one to fetch, pull and push.
remotes.footer: Fetch updates the remote branches; prune also drops the ones deleted on the remote.
remotes.removeBody: The remote and its remote-tracking branches are removed from this repository; nothing changes on {name} itself.
remotes.pushRejected: {remote} has commits that {branch} does not have. Pull them, then push again.
remotes.repositoryChanged: {name} is no longer the open repository: open it again to do this.
remotes.pushRejectedAmend: {remote} holds the commit you amended: pushing its replacement to {branch} needs a forced push, which the commit box does not do.

pullDialog.rebase: Rebase the local commits on top instead of merging
pullDialog.bodyInto: Pulls {from} into {branch}. A pull that stops on conflicts opens the changes screen.

pushTag.title: Push tag {tag}

deleteOnRemote.title: Delete {name} on {remote}?
deleteOnRemote.body: {name} leaves {remote} for everyone who uses it. The toast keeps the commit it pointed at and the command that puts it back while the commit exists.

remotes.deleteStale: {name} moved or left {remote} since the last fetch, so nothing was deleted. Fetch and prune, then try again.
remotes.pullDiverged: {branch} and {upstream} diverged, so nothing was pulled: Pull… pulls with a merge or a rebase.

sync.pushCount: Push, {n} commit to send | Push, {n} commits to send

refused.readingRemotes: The remotes are still being read.
